summary: This Wikipedia-derived note lists New York Yankees team records. It highlights MLB and American League single-season records held by Babe Ruth, Joe DiMaggio and Jack Chesbro, and counts franchise records by player, with Babe Ruth holding the most (16) and Derek Jeter second among hitters (eight). It also gives a table of Yankees career batting records with the player, the figure and the years played for the team.
one_line: Catalog of New York Yankees franchise and MLB record holders, including career batting and pitching marks for Babe Ruth, Derek Jeter and Whitey Ford.
key_facts: Babe Ruth holds MLB single-season records for extra-base hits and total bases.
Babe Ruth holds four other American League single-season records.
Joe DiMaggio had a 56-game hitting streak in the 1941 season, which remains an MLB record.
Jack Chesbro holds three AL records that he set in 1904: games won, games started and complete games.
Babe Ruth holds the most Yankees franchise records, with 16.
Derek Jeter has the second-most Yankees records among hitters, with eight.
Whitey Ford has the most Yankees records among pitchers, with five, all of which are career totals.
Babe Ruth's Yankees career batting average was .349 from 1920 to 1934, and his career on-base percentage was .484.
Babe Ruth's Yankees career slugging percentage was .711 and his on-base plus slugging was 1.195.
Babe Ruth's Yankees career totals include 659 home runs, 1,959 runs, 1,852 walks and 5,131 total bases.
Derek Jeter's Yankees career totals from 1995 to 2014 include 3,465 hits, 2,595 singles, 544 doubles and 358 stolen bases.
Derek Jeter has 12,602 Yankees career plate appearances and 2,747 career games played.
Lou Gehrig's Yankees career totals from 1923 to 1939 include 1,995 runs batted in and 163 triples.
